title: Who can read and download ZPA audit logs
aliases: who can download zpa audit logs

prose.text: Reading the audit log depends on the admin's Private Access role.
What a custom role needs to manage log streaming, and how fast a role change applies, are not sourced {{gap:log-streaming-permission}} {{gap:role-change-delay}}.

checks.do: Whether the admin holds the Private Access Administrator role when the Download option is missing.
Whether a custom role exists and was created by an admin with equal or greater privileges.
What the role's Log Streaming permission is before assuming it governs receiver access.

predefined-roles.statement: Private Access has two predefined admin roles: ZPA Administrator, with read, add, edit and delete privileges, and ZPA Read Only Administrator, with read privileges only.

quotes: ZPA Administrator: An admin with this role has read, add, edit, and delete privileges in the Zscaler Admin Console.
ZPA Read Only Administrator: An admin with this role only has read privileges in the Zscaler Admin Console.

custom-roles.statement: An admin with ZPA Administrator privileges can create custom admin roles for specific Private Access features, and can manage and add only custom roles with equal or lower privileges than their own.

quotes: If you are an admin that has ZPA Administrator privileges, you can also create a custom admin role for your organization.
You can only manage and add custom admin roles with an equal or lower level of privileges than your own.
custom roles (i.e., roles with access to specific Private Access features)

csv-role.statement: Only admins with the Private Access Administrator role can download audit logs from the Audit Logs page.

quotes: Only admins with the Private Access Administrator role can download audit logs.

csv-contents.statement: The downloaded CSV holds only the records for the selected time range and filters, lists timestamps in UTC whatever the account time setting is, and separates the content of the Post-Configuration Change Value column with a dollar sign.

quotes: The CSV file only includes audit log records for the time range and filters specified.
The time displayed is based on the time you choose for your account setting in the Zscaler Admin Console, but the exported CSV file (audit.csv) always lists the timestamp in UTC.
Also, the Post-Configuration Change Value column within the CSV file uses a dollar sign ($) to separate the content within a cell.

log-streaming-permission.title: Log Streaming feature permission
log-streaming-permission.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "The **Log Streaming** feature permission controls access to the LSS configuration UI and API. Admins without Log Streaming permission cannot create or modify LSS receivers." The Private Access roles article names predefined roles and custom roles for specific features but does not list a Log Streaming permission or say what it governs. A partial source is the microtenant configuration permissions table: it has rows for "Log Receivers" (Full for the Default Microtenant, Read only for a custom Microtenant) and "Audit Logs" (Full, Not visible), which show permissions on those objects but not a role feature permission.

role-change-delay.title: How long a role change takes to apply
role-change-delay.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Role changes in ZPA take up to **2 minutes** to take effect." No captured Private Access role article states a delay.
